title: Apple Urges Injunction to Block OpenAI: Former Executive Takes Trade Secrets to the iPhone Throne May Be Threatened

content_html:
Apple filed a request with a U.S. court on Monday local time for a preliminary injunction to prohibit two former employees and OpenAI from obtaining, using, or disclosing confidential information allegedly belonging to Apple, while advancing its trade secret infringement lawsuit. In documents submitted to the court, Apple warned: "If the court does not issue a preliminary injunction, Apple will suffer irreparable harm."

The dispute originated from Apple's lawsuit last month against OpenAI and two former employees who have since joined OpenAI. Apple accused them of stealing trade secrets to help OpenAI advance its consumer hardware business. Among the two former employees involved, Liu Chang was a senior systems electrical engineer at Apple, and Tang Tan served as vice president of product design for the iPhone and Apple Watch—both key figures in Apple's core hardware team.

Accelerated Discovery + Widespread Subpoenas, Apple is Launching a Blitzkrieg

To quickly secure evidence, Apple simultaneously filed a motion to expedite the discovery process, requesting the defendants to provide documents related to alleged access to Apple's proprietary information. Apple also requested the court to schedule pretrial depositions of Liu Chang and Tang Tan, and asked Peng Yuting, an OpenAI employee, and another unidentified former Apple employee now working at OpenAI to testify. Additionally, corporate representatives from OpenAI and its commercial hardware division, io Products—also named as defendants in this case—were also required to be questioned.

OpenAI quickly responded late Monday in a blog post, calling Apple's injunction request "based on incorrect information and entirely unnecessary," and stating, "we do not and have no desire to possess any of Apple's trade secrets." This lawsuit comes at a time when OpenAI has just successfully repelled a legal challenge from Elon Musk's xAI, increasing the pressure of fighting on two fronts.

The implications of this lawsuit go beyond trade secrets themselves. Analysts believe that OpenAI is developing a smartphone or other consumer hardware products, which could potentially no longer rely on traditional applications or operating systems. If successful, consumers' attention might shift away from Apple's best-selling iPhone—something Apple certainly will not allow to grow unchecked under its nose.

content_html_zh:
苹果于当地时间周一向美国法院提出请求，要求颁布初步禁令，禁止两名前员工和 OpenAI 获取、使用或披露据称属于苹果的机密信息，同时推进其商业秘密侵权诉讼。 苹果在提交给法院的文件中警告称：“如果法院不发布初步禁令，苹果将遭受无法弥补的伤害。”

这场纠纷源于苹果上个月对 OpenAI 以及两名后来加入 OpenAI 的前员工提起的诉讼。 苹果指控他们窃取商业机密，以帮助 OpenAI 推进其消费硬件业务。 涉案的两名前员工中，刘畅曾任苹果公司高级系统电气工程师，唐探则担任iPhone和Apple Watch产品设计副总裁，两人都是苹果核心硬件团队的关键人物。

加速发现+广泛传票，苹果正在发起闪电战

为了快速获取证据，苹果公司同时提出了一项加快发现过程的动议，要求被告提供与涉嫌访问苹果专有信息相关的文件。 苹果还要求法院安排刘畅和唐探的审前证词，并要求 OpenAI 员工彭宇婷以及另一名现在 OpenAI 工作的身份不明的前苹果员工出庭作证。 此外，OpenAI 及其商业硬件部门 io Products 的企业代表（也被列为本案被告）也被要求接受讯问。

OpenAI 周一晚间在一篇博文中迅速做出回应，称苹果的禁令请求“基于不正确的信息，完全没有必要”，并表示“我们没有也不想拥有苹果的任何商业秘密。” 此次诉讼发生之际，OpenAI 刚刚成功击退了埃隆·马斯克 (Elon Musk) 的 xAI 的法律挑战，增加了两线作战的压力。

这起诉讼的影响超出了商业秘密本身。 分析师认为，OpenAI 正在开发智能手机或其他消费硬件产品，这些产品可能不再依赖传统应用程序或操作系统。 如果成功，消费者的注意力可能会从苹果最畅销的 iPhone 上转移——苹果肯定不会允许这种现象在自己眼皮子底下肆意发展。
